title: Extension through a scalar-extension map with finite kernel, up to finite rank over the base field
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $V$ be a $k$-vector space, and let $W,M$ be $K$-vector spaces regarded also as $k$-vector spaces by restriction of scalars. Let $\phi:K\otimes_k V\to W$ be $K$-linear, where scalar extension is as in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. Assume $\ker\phi$ is finite dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. For every $k$-linear map $\ell:V\to M$ there exist a $K$-linear map $g:W\to M$ and a finite subset $f\subseteq M$ such that $\ell(v)-g(\phi(1\otimes v))\in\operatorname{span}_k(f)$ for every $v\in V$. Here the span consists of finite $k$-linear combinations of elements of $f$.

source.place: Tag 07FG, proof paragraphs choosing J0 and extending the independent differential images; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FG. The linear-algebra argument is stated for general vector spaces.

proof.text: Choose a k-basis b of V by Module.Free.chooseBasis. Its scalar extension B=b.baseChange K is a K-basis of K tensor_k V, by Mathlib Module.Basis.baseChange.

By Submodule.FG.of_finite, choose a finite set t spanning ker(phi). Put s equal to the union of the supports of B.repr(z) for z in t. Module.Basis.mem_span_image shows each generator belongs to span_K(B(s)), and Submodule.span_le gives ker(phi) contained in that span.

The B-images of s and its complement span disjoint subspaces by LinearIndependent.disjoint_span_image. Restrict the basis to the complement and apply LinearIndependent.map, using this disjointness and the kernel bound. Hence the phi-images of the complementary basis elements are independent.

Module.Basis.span gives a basis of the span of those images. Its constr map sends phi(B_j) to ell(b_j). LinearMap.exists_extend extends this map to a K-linear g on W; evaluation of the extension identity gives g(phi(B_j))=ell(b_j) outside s.

The map delta(v)=ell(v)-g(phi(1 tensor v)) is k-linear by scalar-tower compatibility. Let f be the finite image of s under j maps to delta(b_j). Each delta(b_j) lies in span_k(f): for j in s it is a generator, and outside s it is zero. Since b spans V, Submodule.span_le applied to the inverse image of span_k(f) proves the assertion for every v.

proof_origin.place: General linear-algebra version of the finite-support argument of Tag 07FG, proved in Lean from Mathlib.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_extension_finite_error
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (W : Type x) [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] [Module K W] [IsScalarTower k K W]
    (M : Type y) [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] [Module K M] [IsScalarTower k K M]
    (phi : K ⊗[k] V →ₗ[K] W) (hphi : Module.Finite K phi.ker)
    (ell : V →ₗ[k] M) :
    ∃ (g : W →ₗ[K] M) (f : Finset M),
      ∀ v : V, ell v - g (phi (1 ⊗ₜ[k] v)) ∈ Submodule.span k (f : Set M)
